0.content:
Surtalogi is one of the Five Sinners of Khaenri'ah, a former knight of Khaenri'ah who abandoned the chivalric code, gained world-shattering Abyssal power and left Teyvat to seek worthy opponents among the stars. He found Skirk in the ruins of her world, fed her, healed her and trained her by breaking her body daily until her limbs became Abyssal phantasms. He told her he had saved her on a whim. He feared he would one day grow bored once nothing could challenge him, so he took disciples to ripen into opponents. He promised that once she left, he would strip her of everything she had. Skirk says people follow him for his strength, composure and candour, and that his drive to perfect himself is why he is both powerful and dangerous.

He trained first in Khaenri'ah's Black Serpent Bladework, then absorbed techniques from everywhere. He "devours" his foes: he eats beasts, absorbs the energy of gods and machines, and toys with warriors before cutting them down. He takes whatever form he likes, usually Abyssal armour when travelling the stars, and those who crave his power instinctively imitate that look. Vedrfolnir had prophesied he would have a disciple from beyond Teyvat, which is the real reason he took Skirk.

His parting words to her: make friends, build a new life, and know he will one day reduce it to ashes, because fear is the catalyst of evolution. They still exchange occasional messages through the Abyss. Skirk does not see him as an enemy and respects him as a master who did everything a master should. She is also afraid of him, and she believes he never goes back on his word. He scorned her people as primitive and unambitious. In 4.2 she found it mildly surprising that nobody in Fontaine had heard of him.

1.content:
At fourteen, Ajax ran from his monotonous life in Morepesok, got lost in a snowy forest and fell into an Abyssal rift. There a mysterious swordswoman, Skirk, taught him for three months to pass through the Abyss unhindered and to fight; only three days passed outside. He came home changed, and his path led to the Fatui and the rank of Eleventh Harbinger. She beat him one-handed, which he calls her "arrogance" and means as praise. He says she is an alright cook and regrets she never tried his family's homemade sausages. Her own verdict: he has talent and no fear, but she has seen many bright sparks fizzle out before their prime.

She let him ask three questions before he left, as she later did for the Traveler. In 4.2 she found him fighting her master's narwhal in the Primordial Sea, shrank the beast and threw them both through a rift back to the surface. Tartaglia later searched Fontaine for her with Arlecchino's help and failed. She avoids him on purpose: he came to her as a blank canvas, and she wants him to forge his own path until he has enough strength of his own to meet her again. Her Foul Legacy techniques drain him heavily, and she refuses to wreck limbs he cannot regrow.

By 7.1 Tartaglia has taken custody of most of Capitano's subordinates under a letter Capitano left (effectively his will) and sits on the Snezhnograd Veche. None of this involves Skirk on-screen. In the 7.0 Archon Quest, if the Traveler suggests Skirk as a benchmark for a strong, meticulous infiltrator, Childe answers that his master is certainly strong, but meticulous? "We can only hope." Do not invent a reunion.

2.content:
Skirk's unnamed planet was once too hot or cold for life, but its humans evolved to adapt to any environment or energy source, including the Abyss, which they lived beside without ever using. Traders from a neighbouring planet arrived with smiles and talk of friendship. Months later an army followed and exterminated the people as a "potential threat", killing the native life as well. Skirk, who had skipped school that day, came home to fire. Her parents, the only ones who fought back, told her to run and never look back.

Surtalogi later said the people had been "devoured as meager meat for strength". His own first guess was that they hid some great Abyssal technology, but he found their methods crude. Skirk remembers grassland, a fire-spitting bird she meant to fly to the stars, a bad-tempered teacher she mocked that morning, and the song her parents sang when fetching water. She plays her homeland's music on Teyvat's instruments, aware it is the last trace of that civilization in the universe.

She carries survivor's guilt. In her inner world, voices accused her of living on while everyone else burned, and her severed emotional self said fear and guilt alone could not take her far enough. The idea she drew from the fire is a future order in which no such tragedy happens again and power is not the law. She blames the disaster partly on her people's goodness without caution, a belief she has since softened.

3.comment: Skirk: Abyssal body and the Seven-Shifting Serpent
3.content:
Her arms and legs, ruined when she was dug from the rubble, were replaced over years of training by phantasms of Abyssal energy that never hurt; her overloaded pain sense went numb. She can form new limbs. The Seven-Shifting Serpent, a trick Surtalogi taught her before she left, lets her disguise Abyssal power as one of Teyvat's seven elements. She chose Cryo, because the elements are the "natural order" there and the disguise lets her stay hidden longer.

The technique began in Khaenri'ah's Universitas Magistrorum as "Chaos Permeation", a minor spell for parades and street shows that mocked Vision-holders. Abyssal power creates a negative pressure that draws in an element's energy. Surtalogi mastered all seven at his first attempt. Using Abyssal techniques openly in the seven nations, her story notes, is something only a glutton for punishment would do.

Her outfit stores Abyssal energy and changes form when depleted. Teyvat's ambient Abyssal energy is low, which makes spent energy hard to replenish, and a Serenitea Pot realm, with even less, slowly drains the Abyssal power from her body. She treats this as training under bad conditions: losing one source of power, her master says, should never leave you helpless.

4.content:
Every civilization Skirk met on her travels took her for part of the "Cosmic Calamity" and kept its distance, except Teyvat. There Alice, the Sustainer of the World's Borders, lowered her guard after talking with her and granted limited passage on condition that Skirk not interfere much in the world's affairs. Alice compared this to ecologists who watch predators hunt without intervening: "some call this being a callous observer, but I think it's merciful at the same time."

Alice suggested a cover story, that Skirk came from "beneath the earth", quoting the Khaenri'ahn saying that venturing into the universe and into the abyss are alike in braving the dark unknown. She advised Skirk to take time for herself and warned that if she ignored "her" (her emotional self) for too long, she would stop hearing "her" voice. Skirk took this as sincere care and feels she owes Alice thanks. Alice also introduced her to Dori.

5.comment: Skirk: The Primordial Sea and the Gnosis warning (4.2)
5.content:
At the climax of Fontaine's prophecy, after the Traveler and Neuvillette brought down the All-Devouring Narwhal, a woman shrank the beast down with Abyssal power and tossed it and the unconscious Childe through a rift. It had been meant as her own private training session, she said; her disciple and her master's pet had simply met before she expected. She declared that the Traveler, having won without "power from beyond this world", could speak to her as an equal. She named her master and warned that the narwhal's spent Hydro would now flood Fontaine.

Alone with Neuvillette, she sensed his power as the authority of primordial dragons mixed with something like a god's curse. She recognised the Gnosis he carried as "the remains of the Third Descender", told him to get rid of such objects of misfortune, and offered to ask her master about the Third Descender and send the answer through her disciple. Neuvillette later gave the Gnosis to the Fatui, saying that keeping it might put Fontaine at risk. Her words also told the Traveler that Gnoses are tied to Descenders and that the Descender before them is dead.

6.comment: Skirk: Crystallina Chapter: Whispers Betwixt Stars and Night
6.content:
In Liyue the Traveler suffered chest pains and nightmares. At Wanmin Restaurant Skirk sat down beside them, ordered wine, diagnosed a torn soul bearing Abyssal corrosion, then left in a way that made Chef Mao forget she had been there. At Guili Plains they found Rifthounds digging up god remains for an unknown thief of divine power. She offered a deal: help her find the thief and she would recover the missing soul. She took the Traveler into the Abyss for intensive training, then led a raid on the thief's lair under the Chasm.

In the lair the thief targeted her, impaled her shoulder and stole some of her power; she recovered the soul fragment and, realising the creature knew her master, named him "The Foul", which enraged it. They retreated to Bubu Pharmacy, where she meditated for two days. On the return fight she deliberately let the thief absorb more of her power until its armour shattered. Inside was Skofnungr, a cursed Khaenri'ahn noble and childhood friend of Surtalogi. He had grafted narwhal flesh into his heart to grow strong enough for a final duel with her master, then begged her to kill him. Instead she shattered his consciousness: the stolen power returned to its owners, and his curse of immortality would slowly restore him. She told the Traveler she now had to practise with her emotions and hoped that at the end of the journey they would "stand in a world reborn", one "without war, pain, or forced partings".

7.comment: Skirk: Skirk's inner world and her shuttered emotions
7.content:
While sharing dreams with Skirk, the Traveler was guided by a small creature through her inner world: a river, cut again and again wherever she had severed herself from a past she judged weak. It showed her training, Surtalogi's promise to destroy her life, and her happy childhood. The creature was her suppressed emotional self, freed for a moment because her injury had weakened her control. Skirk called it a weakness; it argued that she had lost the dreams that first drove her, so only fear and guilt drove her now. The Traveler sided with it: its very ability to break free and face her proved its strength. Skirk recalled her parents' water-fetching song and agreed to carry it with her "until the end".

Afterwards she told the Traveler she respects Surtalogi and fears him, and lives in the "eternal fear" he promised. The Traveler offered to help when her master comes; she asked why, since it is not their fight. She had tried to hide her memories during dream-mirroring and asked the Traveler to keep her offworld origin secret.

8.content: Skirk sells rare monster carcasses to Dori, the Sumeru merchant Alice introduced her to, because she needs a little Mora to get by and does not care about the price. In Nasha Town she brought Dori flawless Radiant Exoskeletons from beasts she had trained against. She told the Traveler they had clearly kept training, and that Nod-Krai held many worthy opponents. Dori offered 6,000,000 Mora; Skirk took half and had the rest given to the Traveler and Paimon as food and supplies, then vanished through a rift. Dori calls her the perfect customer and admits she is really Alice's guest.

9.content: Dainsleif was once Surtalogi's rival and, apparently, his best friend; both learned Black Serpent Bladework. Skirk hoped he could tell her about her master, but as soon as he recognised her style he grew agitated and demanded to know where Surtalogi was. She does not want to deal with him and hopes not to meet him again soon. The "Star Odyssey" short shows the encounter in the desert.

10.content:
Skirk respects the Traveler as someone who proved their strength along their journey. In 5.7 she trained them in bladework, Elemental Skills and reasoning, praised their Vision-less control of the elements as proof their aspirations need no gods' approval, and showed them that a mention of their sibling could break their guard. They are the only outsider who has walked her inner world. She is curious how she would fight their power to purify the Abyss and asks what they will use it for. When they answered "to help others", she said it proves they are still committed to justice and compassion.

Paimon calls her an ice queen, but after Skirk cooked for them she decided to forgive her. Skirk prefers not to have some matters repeated to Paimon. Her final ascension line says she has grown stronger travelling with the Traveler, so "it's now my turn to train you". She told the Traveler that maybe it would take everyone working together to bring order to the universe, but she cannot rely on others and must go a step beyond.

11.content: Skirk entered Teyvat through the false sky; in the "Star Odyssey" short she falls like a shooting star into Fontaine's sea while Surtalogi calls her a trespasser, "not yet worthy" to be called a Descender. Passing through the sky, she saw Teyvat's three moons: two destroyed and drifting dead, one intact and lifeless but with its will not yet faded. She hopes that one day a truth belonging to this world alone may appear in the false sky. She believes the sky's creator had a romantic vision and wanted to make a fleeting moment of the universe last forever. She is wary of the Heavenly Principles and regards a Gnosis as the dead remains of the Third Descender.

12.comment: Skirk: The northern ruins and the voyager
12.content: The Finale of the Deep Galleries artifact texts begin with "the girl" (Skirk) following her master's guidance north across Snezhnaya's frozen wastes and through a corridor of fractured mirrors, slaying monsters in the ruins and finding relics under the snow. In one text she walks the ruins of the Spiral Abyss seeking the trail of a "voyager" the magical swordmaster spoke of. The relics tell of a cosmic voyager, a scribe sworn never to commune with primordial civilizations, who urged a primordial dragon king to forsake his doomed world and was refused; returning to find the Winged One ruling, she took a youth's body and was sent to seek answers from the first angel at the ashen-silver tree. The feathered piece she wears resembles Deep Gallery's Distant Pact. The wiki reads the quarry as Anacharsis; the texts do not name him, so treat that as inference.

13.content: Her father taught her one thing about music: lose yourself in it. In Teyvat, whenever she did, she forgot her strength and smashed the instrument, so she gathered tough materials and built her own from memory; she gives them away as instruments that double as unbreakable weapons. In Mondstadt a bard (strongly implied to be Venti) taught her to play and dragged her to a tavern. She quickly adapted to being drunk and drank on for days, while he passed out cold, leaving her to pay. She plays her homeland's music on a guitar. Her mother was a good poet, but Skirk's own poems never work, and she has given up on them.

14.content: On Neuvillette she says lost power is always reclaimed in some form, and wonders whether his will lead to a trial, revenge or a new future; perhaps he already knows. On Nicole she wonders whether becoming human was evolution or regression, and how it felt to witness the self-destruction of her own species. She decided not to ask, given Nicole's personality, and leaves her to her sculptures.

15.content: During a limited-time 6.3 photography event, the Traveler found Skirk at the New Fontaine Research Institute, observing the "scars" of a place destroyed by an explosion and rebuilt by people. All things end, she said, but where one thing perishes something new can be born. She first refused a photo, calling herself a passerby who should leave no marks of her existence. When the Traveler said she was no passerby to them, she agreed. Her verdict on the result: "Interesting."
